chunks.text: Whether you are going to watch a sports game, a concert or another event, this episode will help you feel more comfortable.
I will teach you useful words, common phrases and important questions that you can use at the stadium.
Visiting a stadium can be exciting, but it might also feel confusing if you don't know how to speak the language well.
But don't worry.
After this episode, you will feel more confident when talking to people at the stadium.
Part one, common words at the stadium.
First, let's learn some important words that you will hear at the stadium.
I will say each word slowly and you can repeat after me.
Types of places at the stadium, stadium, a large building where sports games and other events take place.

Seating section, the area where you sit to watch the event, concessions, the places where you can buy food and drinks, restrooms, the bathrooms at the stadium, box office, the place where you can buy tickets, people at the stadium, fan, a person who supports a sports team or artist, athlete, a person who plays sports, team, a group of athletes playing together in a sport, referee, the person who makes sure the rules of the game are followed, security, the people who make sure everyone is safe at the stadium, sports equipment and terms, ball, a round object used in many sports, goal, the area where the ball needs to go in many sports like soccer or basketball, scoreboard, a board that shows the points or score of the game, halftime, the break between the two halves of the game, cheering, the act of shouting and clapping to support a team, part two, useful phrases at the stadium.
Now let's practice some useful phrases.
I will say each phrase twice.
Listen carefully and repeat after me.
Asking for directions at the stadium.
Where is my seating section?
How do I get to the restroom?
Where can I buy food?
Where is the box office?
Can you help me find my seat?
Talking about the game or event.
What time does the game start?
Who is playing today?
What's the score?
Is there a halftime show?
Who won the last game?
Buying tickets or merchandise?
How much is a ticket?
Can I buy a ticket here?
Do you have any team merchandise?
How much are the t -shirts?
Can I pay with a credit card?
Asking about the schedule.
When does the next game start?
What other events are happening today?
Is there a concert after the game?
When does the stadium open?
How long does the event last?
Part three, common situations at the stadium.
Let's now talk about different situations you might experience at the stadium.
I will describe the situation and give you some sentences that you can use.
One, finding your seat.
You arrive at the stadium and you need to find your seat.
Excuse me, where is section A?
Is this seat 10B?
Can I sit in the front row?
Where are the best seats for this game?
Two, buying food or drinks.
You are hungry and want to buy something to eat.
What do you have to eat?
Can I get a hot dog and a soda?
How much is a popcorn?
Is there water available?
Do you accept credit cards?
Three, talking about the game.
You are watching the game and want to talk about what is happening.
That was a great goal.
Who is winning?
The referee made a bad call.
This game is so exciting.
I can't believe they scored.
Four, asking for help or information.
You need help or information at the stadium.
Where is the nearest exit?
Can you tell me when the game is over?
Is there a lost and found here?
How do I get to the parking lot?
Are pets allowed in the stadium?
Part four, summary and practice.
Great job.
Today we learned many important words and phrases for the stadium.
Let's review important words.
Stadium, seating section, concessions, restroom, box office, fan, athlete, referee, security, scoreboard, halftime cheering.
Common phrases, asking for directions, talking about the game, buying tickets or food, asking about the schedule.
Situations at the stadium, finding your seat, buying food, talking about the game, asking for help or information.
Now try to practice these sentences.
Imagine you are at the stadium and repeat the phrases.
You can listen to this episode again to improve your pronunciation and confidence.
Thank you for listening to Slow English Podcast.
